The comparison examines the distribution of the [[cha2ds2-vasc|CHA2DS2-VASc]] score among prevalent patients with atrial fibrillation who subsequently experienced an intracranial bleed, broken down by the five Danish regions and the national total for [[danmark|Danmark]]. This metric is critical for understanding the baseline stroke and bleeding risk profiles of patients who ultimately suffered one of the most severe bleeding complications.

In terms of absolute volume, [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] recorded the highest number of these cases among the regions with 205 patients, closely followed by [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] with 196 patients [^src1]. [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] reported the fewest cases with 104 patients [^src1]. Nationally, there were 797 prevalent atrial fibrillation patients who developed an intracranial bleed [^src1].

When analyzing the risk score distribution, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] emerges as a distinct outlier. It has the highest regional proportion of patients with a score of 2 (38.5%) and a score of 3 (34.6%) [^src1]. Together, these two mid-range scores account for 73.1% of all intracranial bleeding cases in the region, a significantly heavier concentration than in [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], where scores of 2 and 3 account for 53.0% of cases [^src1]. Conversely, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] has the lowest proportion of patients with a baseline score of 0 (4.8%), while [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] has the highest regional proportion at 9.8% [^src1].

Furthermore, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] is the only region that recorded zero patients (0%) at the maximum score of 7, whereas the national data shows that 0.6% of patients (5 individuals) fell into this highest risk category before their intracranial bleed [^src1]. 

Because the available evidence consists of a single dated section from the 2025 report, no longitudinal trends can be established regarding whether regional risk profiles for this specific complication are improving, declining, or remaining flat over time.
